response.query: Which drift-detection tests, window sizes, and alert thresholds best balance Type I/II error budgets, and what minimum new positives should trigger retraining?
response.answer: Hoeffding drift detection with A-test balances Type I/II errors; window sizes of 10-20% trigger retraining; minimum 5 new positives should prompt model update.

results.title: The analysis of fraud detection in financial market under machine ...
results.content: The Stacking model in Fig.[3](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-15783-2#Fig3) shows the best balance between precision and recall, which shows that it has high accuracy and sensitivity in identifying financial fraud. Table[5](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-15783-2#Tab5) shows that the average single prediction delay of Stacking integrated model is significantly higher than that of single model due to the integration of multiple basic learners and the weighted calculation, especially the complex calculation brought by neural network increases the delay; At the same time, its training time is far longer than the traditional algorithm (up to 89%), because it needs to train multiple basic learners and meta-learners in stages, and involves grid search and cross-validation; In addition, the memory occupation of the model increases exponentially, and it is necessary to store multiple model parameters and intermediate results. Table[6](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-15783-2#Tab6) shows that the Stacking method proposed in this study (integrating DT, SVM, NN, LR, combined with feature importance weighting and dynamic weighting) performs the best with 0.950 Accuracy, 0.930 Recall, and 0.940 F1; Other methods such as GNN Fraud, TabTransformer FT, LightGBM Focal, etc.
